comments.author: home
comments.text:
Naming convention settled: the open-source core product repository becomes
AnthusAI/Chatticus (no dot) — the product name, not the domain. The new
private marketing/SaaS repository is AnthusAI/Chattic.us-web (with the dot,
after the domain it serves). This distinguishes "the product" from "the
domain that sells it," matching the Organization/Account split elsewhere in
this epic.

This is a deliberate, separately-confirmed action, not bundled into the
marketing split itself — do not execute the actual GitHub rename as a side
effect of other work in this epic.

What the rename touches, beyond the GitHub UI action:

- infra/lib/github-deploy-stack.ts hardcodes the repo name into the AWS OIDC
  trust policy: GITHUB_REPOSITORY = "AnthusAI/Chattic.us" and
  GITHUB_SUB_PREFIX = "repo:AnthusAI@152415604/Chattic.us@1350947261". Confirm
  whether GitHub's OIDC sub claim uses the numeric repo id (stable across a
  rename) or the name string (would change) before assuming the trust policy
  survives unchanged — this file's own comment explains why the simpler
  job_workflow_ref condition was rejected, read it before touching this.
- The nine deploy-{web,thinturn,auth}-{development,staging,production}.yml
  workflows and semantic-release.yml reference the repo implicitly via
  actions/checkout and the OIDC role ARN; verify none hardcode the old name.
- Root package.json's "name" field, README badges/links, and any absolute
  github.com/AnthusAI/Chattic.us URLs in docs/.
- The local git remote and any AGENTS.local.md references.
- Chattic.us-web's package.json tarball dependency URL
  (github.com/AnthusAI/<name>/archive/...) must point at whichever name is
  live at the time Chattic.us-web is stood up (task 9c5d32) — sequence this
  rename before or after that task deliberately, not accidentally.

GitHub's rename redirect covers git clone/fetch/push and web URLs
automatically, but does not cover string comparisons in IAM trust policies or
hardcoded config.

**Done when:** a production deploy workflow run succeeds post-rename, proving
the OIDC trust policy still resolves.
